title: Polynomial time for split-word computation
statement: For every pair of natural numbers $C,c$, there exist a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet and a natural number $A$ such that, on every binary input of length $n$, the machine computes the split word in exactly $A(n+1)^{c+2}$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: Existence of a finite binary-alphabet Turing machine
The time bound is $A(n+1)^{c+2}$ for every input length $n$
replaced:
For all constants $C, c$ there exist a finite machine and a constant $A$
computing the split-word function (the paired prefix/suffix encoding, or the
empty failure word) within time $A (n + 1)^{c+2}$ on inputs of length $n$.
